methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical mechanistic and orthotopic model study using two thyroid cancer cell lines (K1 PTC, 8505C ATC) with in vitro cytotoxicity (CCK-8), OATP inhibitor uptake studies (BSP, MK-571, 4 degC), and orthotopic nu/nu mouse models (n=5 for K1, n=10 for 8505C) with sequential PBS washes, multistep FGS, and H&E validation. Appropriate controls and histologic correlation with fluorescence provide reasonable internal validity. Limitations include small sample sizes, no blinded histologic assessment, no randomization details, single institution, ex vivo FGS performed after euthanasia (rather than live surgical model), and no orthotopic PDX or indolent-disease model to test specificity. The study acknowledges these and the limitations of using cell line xenografts. Statistical approach is appropriate (Friedman, pairwise Wilcoxon, paired t on log-transformed data with geometric mean ratios), with normality assessment, though no sample-size justification is provided and multiplicity for multiple TBR comparisons is handled conservatively.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical orthotopic mouse model study (Oxford LoE 5). The translational rationale is strong given the established clinical significance of microscopic positive surgical margins in thyroid cancer (especially in robotic thyroidectomy and ATC) and the sprayable topical approach's practical appeal. However, the gap from nude mouse ex vivo FGS to clinical use in humans (including Hashimoto thyroiditis coexistence, in vivo thyroid anatomy with tracheal/esophageal proximity, regulatory approval) is substantial, making clinical relevance plausible but unproven.

reporting_quality.justification: For preclinical animal research ARRIVE applies; the paper describes mouse strain, age, source, anesthesia/analgesia, IACUC approval, and cell line sources with ATCC authentication implied. However, ARRIVE is not explicitly referenced; several items are missing including sample-size justification, randomization and blinding details, experimental unit clarification, and reporting of attrition. No data or code availability statement and PH10 synthesis details rely on prior publication. Statistical methods are clearly described, as are outcomes (TBR with SD and paired 95% CI for one comparison).

novelty_literature.justification: The PH10 probe and the sprayable pH-sensitive NIR imaging approach are not new; the same group previously published PH10 application to thyroid cancer in orthotopic models (reference 11, Jaiswal 2025), and pH-sensitive sprayable fluorophores have been applied to liver, colon, ovarian, and prostate tumors (references cited). The novel contribution here is extending PH10 to multistep FGS for identifying microscopic positive surgical margins and validating in the aggressive 8505C ATC model. Meaningful but incremental extension rather than a first-in-class methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is well organized and clearly written with structured methods, logically presented results progressing from in vitro to in vivo, and a thoughtful discussion connecting findings to robotic thyroidectomy and ATC clinical needs. Figures are clearly described and referenced (cytotoxicity, OATP inhibition, TBRs, FGS steps, H&E validation). Limitations are explicitly acknowledged including cell line aggressiveness, non-biomarker-specific mechanism, Hashimoto thyroiditis coexistence, and preclinical-to-clinical gap. Some minor phrasing issues but overall publication-quality.

key_strengths: Orthotopic surgical implantation model rather than subcutaneous xenograft, providing anatomically relevant thyroid location
Validation across both PTC (K1) and aggressive ATC (8505C) cell lines with mechanistic OATP inhibitor evidence for selective uptake
Multistep FGS with H&E histopathologic correlation demonstrating both macroscopic and microscopic margin detection
Clinical relevance framed around robotic thyroidectomy where tactile feedback is limited, a genuine unmet need
Appropriate use of nonparametric statistics (Friedman, pairwise Wilcoxon) and paired log-transformed analyses with geometric mean ratios
key_concerns: Small sample sizes (n=5 K1, n=10 8505C), no reported sample-size justification, randomization, or blinded histologic scoring
Ex vivo FGS after euthanasia rather than true live surgical model limits translation; no in vivo perfusion dynamics, bleeding, or thermal-artifact conditions tested
Heavy reliance on same-group prior publication (Jaiswal 2025) for probe characterization and orthotopic SOI methodology, making novelty modestly incremental
No explicit ARRIVE checklist adherence, no data/code availability, and PH10 chemical synthesis details not provided in this manuscript
No assessment in PDX or indolent thyroid cancer models; generalizability to well-differentiated low-proliferating tumors is unproven
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent preclinical validation study extending a previously published sprayable fluorescent probe to microscopic margin detection in thyroid cancer orthotopic models; appropriate for a Tier 3 oncology journal with minor revisions to strengthen ARRIVE reporting and acknowledge the incremental nature of the contribution.
